source_title: Unlawful Use of an Unmanned Aircraft System
regulated_activity: Using a UAS to conduct surveillance of, gather evidence or collect information about, or photographically/electronically record 'critical infrastructure' (defined to include electrical generation/delivery systems, petroleum refineries, chemical/rubber manufacturing facilities, petroleum/chemical storage, railroad operating facilities, communication towers, food processing/manufacturing facilities, and correctional/detention facilities) without the owner's prior written consent
requirement_type: Prohibition (misdemeanor), with property-owner and retained-contractor exceptions
summary: Ark. Code Ann. § 5-60-103 makes it a Class B misdemeanor (Class A for a second or subsequent offense) to knowingly use a UAS to conduct surveillance of, gather evidence about, or record critical infrastructure without the owner's prior written consent. The statute's definition of 'unmanned aircraft system' excludes a UAS used under an FAA certificate of authorization (COA) — a specific public-agency authorization instrument, distinct from an ordinary Part 107 remote pilot certificate — as well as UAS used by the federal government, the state (after Governor consultation), or law enforcement/emergency-management agencies for specified purposes. Separately, the statute does not prohibit a property owner (or a third person retained by the owner) from using a UAS to survey, inspect, or record their own property, or property they hold under a lease, servitude, right-of-way, permit, or similar right, nor does it prohibit insurance-related underwriting/damage-investigation use.

uas_topic: Critical infrastructure UAS restriction — civil remedy
summary: Ark. source_title: Crime of Video Voyeurism (Unmanned Vehicle or Aircraft)
regulated_activity: Knowingly using an unmanned vehicle or aircraft (among other listed recording devices) that is concealed, operated to escape detection, or disguised, to secretly/surreptitiously record or view another person's body where that person has a reasonable expectation of privacy, without consent
requirement_type: Prohibition (misdemeanor, elevated if distributed/transmitted or prior conviction)
summary: Ark. Code Ann. § 5-16-101(b) makes it unlawful to knowingly use an unmanned vehicle or aircraft, camcorder, motion picture camera, photographic camera, or other equipment that is concealed, operated to escape detection, or disguised, to secretly or surreptitiously videotape, film, photograph, record, or electronically view another person's body where that person has a reasonable expectation of privacy, without the person's knowledge or consent. A violation is a Class B misdemeanor, elevated to a Class A misdemeanor if the recording is distributed, posted online, or the person has a prior conviction under this section or § 5-16-102 (AR-004). Subsection (d) exempts several categories of authorized monitoring (court-ordered, security monitoring by an occupant/owner/administrator, correctional-facility security monitoring, and law-enforcement monitoring within official duties), none of which are general commercial-UAS-operator exceptions.

source_title: Crime of Voyeurism (Unmanned Vehicle or Aircraft)
regulated_activity: For the purpose of sexual arousal or gratification, using an unmanned vehicle or aircraft to look, without consent, into a private place in a public accommodation where a person may reasonably be expected to be nude/partially nude, or to enter another's private property and look into a dwelling under specified privacy-invading circumstances
requirement_type: Prohibition (misdemeanor to felony depending on victim age/prior conviction)
summary: Ark. Code Ann. § 5-16-102(b) makes it a crime, when done for sexual arousal or gratification, to use (personally or via an unmanned vehicle or aircraft) unconsented viewing into a private place within a public accommodation where nudity/partial nudity may reasonably be expected, or to enter another's private property via a UAS and look into a dwelling unit under specified privacy-invading conditions. Penalties range from a Class A misdemeanor up to a Class C or Class D felony depending on victim age and prior convictions.

source_title: UAS Possession/Operation Restriction for Registered Sex Offenders
regulated_party: Level 3 or Level 4 registered sex offenders
regulated_activity: Purchasing, owning, possessing, using, or operating a UAS
summary: Ark. Code Ann. § 5-14-138 prohibits a person required to register under the Sex Offender Registration Act who has been assessed as a Level 3 or Level 4 offender from purchasing, owning, possessing, using, or operating a UAS, unless use is required as part of the person's employment. A violation is a Class D felony.
